name: Sanitation
overview: Scripture emphasizes the importance of cleanliness and proper disposal in maintaining holiness and health among God's people. Instructions such as burning the flesh, skin, and dung of the bullock outside the camp (Exodus 29:14) and not consuming consecrated food left overnight (Exodus 29:34) highlight God's concern for sanctification through sanitation. Additionally, the command to labor for six days and rest on the seventh (Exodus 20:9; 34:21) reflects a divine rhythm that includes rest as part of God's provision for physical and spiritual well-being.
